Creator Kickstarter · Live Call

Ready, Fire, Aim

And doing the thing you keep avoiding.

The idea

What if the thing you keep putting off is the thing you need to be doing most?

A concept from a guy in a business Skool community. I have been catching myself doing the exact opposite of it.

The sneaky part

Procrastination does not always look like procrastination

When we think of procrastinating, we picture sitting on the couch watching Netflix instead of working.

That is not usually how it happens when you run your own business.

Entrepreneurial procrastination

It can look really productive

You can work eight hours straight and still avoid the one thing that actually matters.

What it looks like on a Tuesday

All of this feels like work

Redesign your website Make Canva graphics Tweak your logo Build a content calendar Research platforms Organize Notion Set up automations Rewrite your About page Watch another course

Every one of them is real work. None of them is the work.

“I worked all day.”

And you did. But did you actually move the business forward?

That is a different question.

Section two

Ready, Fire, Aim

A book by Michael Masterson, and the reason I rethought how I start anything.

The normal saying

Ready. Aim. Fire.

ReadyYou prepare.
→
AimYou line it all up. Carefully.
→
FireAnd finally, once you are confident enough, you go.

The problem is that “confident enough” never quite arrives.

Masterson flips the last two

Ready. Fire. Aim.

ReadyEnough preparation to give yourself a reasonable shot.
→
FireYou actually put it into the world.
→
AimNow you have real information to aim with.

This one is not optional. It is how you make it in business.

To be clear

You still get ready

This is not “I have an idea at breakfast and spend $20,000 launching it before lunch.”

You need enough preparation to give yourself a reasonable shot. That is all.

Then

But then you FIRE

Put the offer out Publish the post Launch the product Email everyone you know Pitch somebody Run the ad
And only then

Now you can really aim

Because now you have information. You have actual feedback.

Before you fire, most of what you are doing is guessing.

Two ways to spend the next month

Still aiming

  • Months deciding what your first social post should be
  • Weeks tweaking the website, the wording, the images, the design, before anyone sees it
  • Forever working out what the offer should be, what is in it, who it is even for
vs

You just fired

  • You publish the post
  • You share the website
  • You talk to people about what you are working on
  • You start having conversations with your audience

One of these produces information. The other produces a nicer guess.

And suddenly

You start getting clues

01

One post takes off

It gets way more engagement than everything else you posted.

02

Someone replies

“This is exactly what I’m struggling with.”

03

The same question

A few people keep asking you the same thing.

04

Half of it lands

They are into one part of your idea and quiet about the rest.

What feedback does

It can completely change the direction you were going in

You thoughtPeople want a course→They want a paid weekly newsletter
You thoughtThis one topic is your main thing→Everyone responds to something else
You thoughtThe breakthrough is a perfect website→It was one imperfect post
The point

Reality gives you better information than your imagination does

You can think and plan and prepare forever. Until you put something into the world, a lot of it is still a guess.

If you are not putting it out there, the only feedback you get is your own. That is a closed loop. There is no real value in it.

Section three

We want certainty before we act

Most of us want to run the whole thing in reverse.

What we want to know first
Will people buy this? Will this post work? What will people think? Is this the right niche? Is this the right price? Course or membership? YouTube or Substack? $500 or $1,000?

And we want someone to tell us the correct answer before we start.

But there is not a correct answer yet. The answer is waiting to reveal itself once you start doing the thing.

Get comfortable saying this

“I don’t know. Let’s find out.”

  • Let’s run it
  • Let’s put it in front of 20 people
  • Let’s publish 10 videos
  • Let’s pitch five clients
  • Let’s send the email
  • Let’s see what happens
not

“I don’t know, so I’m going to think about it for another month.”

  • Another month of reading
  • Another month of planning
  • Another month of no information

Fire. Then aim.

Section four

I have been catching myself doing this

Websites, social media and AI automations for contractors in the US. A different client, so it needs a different approach.

What I did instead

I kept doing the parts I find really easy

It is the stuff we teach in this course, because it is the stuff I know best.

Build the website Tinker with the design Move sections around Change the copy Try a different image Play with AI Set up the socials Build the calendar Build automations
Every single day

“Look what I built.”

And I am making progress. All of it feels fantastic, because all of it is comfortable.

But none of it gets me clients. The website does not make someone buy. A perfectly organized content calendar does not make revenue because it exists.

So I asked

What am I avoiding?

Run paid ads

Not learn about ads. Actually put my credit card in and spend money on them.

Cold outreach

Contact people who are not already following me. Which I hate doing.

Get on the phone

Cold call people. Have awkward conversations.

Get rejected

Sound like an idiot sometimes. Then learn how to get better.

And then it landed

Ohhhh. That is the business.

The website

is not the business

The logo

is not the business

The automation

is not the business

Those things support the business. Until I can get in front of someone with a problem I solve, explain why I can help, and get some of them to pay me, I have not solved the important part.

Section five

Productive procrastination

You are not avoiding work. You are avoiding a specific kind of work by replacing it with easier work.

Why the easy thing always wins

The substitute work

  • It is something you are already good at
  • Doing it feels nice
  • It reinforces your identity. You are competent, you know what you are doing
  • You control the result
vs

The hard thing

  • It comes with uncertainty
  • You do not know what will happen
  • And worse: someone else is going to see it
  • Someone else is going to judge it
That is why we hide in certain tasks
SafeRedesign my homepage→It is all up to me how it turns out
ExposedDial 50 business owners who do not want to hear from me→It is up to them
SafeSpend another week editing the offer→Nobody can reject you
ExposedOpen the doors and ask 100 people to buy it→Now you can be rejected
Section six

Follow the discomfort

The thing you are putting off the most is usually the thing you should do first.

Not every annoying task. But nine times out of ten, yes.

Think about what makes us uncomfortable
Selling Publishing Charging more Following up Making an offer Running an ad Reaching out to someone Asking for the testimonial Going live Talking on camera

They all have one thing in common

They create the possibility of failure. And because they create the possibility of failure, they create the possibility of success.

Both sides of the same coin

Never fire

  • You cannot get rejected if you never make an offer
  • You cannot publish a flop if you never publish
but

And also

  • You cannot make the sale
  • You cannot publish the thing that takes off and changes your life

The uncomfortable tasks are where the feedback lives. And feedback is what lets you aim.

Section seven · write this down

Ask yourself this

If I could only do ONE thing over the next seven days to create revenue or learn something important about my business, what would it be?

Careful, because these are not it

Not

What would make my business prettier?

Not

What would make me feel organized?

Not

What could I check off my list?

Not

What could I learn more about?

What could actually move the needle?

And if that one is hard to answer, try this instead: what is the one thing you KNOW you need to be doing, but you keep putting off?

Section eight

Your challenge this week

Identify your one hard thing. The task that has been hanging around. The thing you keep moving to tomorrow. The thing you find yourself too busy to do.

Then ask

Is this hard because it is complicated?

  • Then learn enough to take the first step
or

Is this hard because the result actually matters to me?

  • Then it is the one. Do it first.

Those are two very different things.

One warning

Do not turn learning into another hiding place

You do not need eleven hours of Facebook Ads tutorials before running a small test
You do not need three books about sales before having a sales conversation
You do not need 400 YouTubers explaining YouTube before posting your first ten videos

Learn enough. Get ready. Then fire.

Make yourself one simple rule

When you sit down at your computer, do the uncomfortable tasks before the comfortable ones. Every single time.

Before Canva Before redesigning Before tinkering Before organizing Before researching Before asking ChatGPT to rewrite the same paragraph twenty-seven ways
Send the email Make the pitch Record the talking head Launch the offer Run the test
And then

Pay attention

What happened?
What did people respond to?
What did not work?
What objections came up?
What surprised you?
What did somebody say that you had not considered?
Great. Now you aim.
FirePut something real into the world.
→
AimRead what the market told you.
→
Fire againThis time you know where to point it.

That is the whole loop. It only starts turning once you fire the first time.

There are no failures.
Only lessons.

Discussion · let’s go around

Three questions

01

What have you been avoiding?

The important thing in your business right now that you know you have been avoiding. Be brutally specific: not “I need to work on marketing”, but “I’ve been avoiding emailing my list and offering my coaching program.”

02

What are you doing instead?

What is your productive procrastination? The things you keep convincing yourself are important because they are easier than the thing you actually need to do.

03

What can you FIRE this week?

Something real. Something that creates feedback. Something where the market gets a vote.

You probably do not need another month of aiming. You need one good shot, so you finally know where to aim next.
